hypotheses.title: Transfer handler reentrancy via callback during finalization
hypotheses.evidence: test_H1_transfer_handler_reentrancy_blocked: ENTERED bit in TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags persists through _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse callbacks. All state-changing entry points check ENTERED bit first, causing revert. CEI pattern in _transferHookFeesByHook decrements storage before safeTransfer.

hypotheses.title: Multi-swap transient storage isolation failure between hops
hypotheses.evidence: test_H2_multiswap_transient_isolation: Two-pool multi-swap verifies each hop computes independently. Reserves update correctly per-hop. Total solvency maintained (AMM balance >= reserves). No cross-hop contamination via transient storage.

hypotheses.title: Native ETH refund reentrancy in _depositWrappedNativeAndRefundExcess
hypotheses.evidence: test_H3_eth_refund_reentrancy: The .call{value} refund at line 3252 happens BEFORE WETH deposit (line 3256), but ENTERED bit is still set from the parent nonReentrantWithFlags guard. Any reentrant call from the refund recipient reverts. Solvency test confirms no value leak.

hypotheses.title: CLOB settlement stale read from transient storage
hypotheses.evidence: test_H4_clob_settlement_no_stale_read: directSwap uses DIRECT_SWAP_GUARD_FLAG which includes SWAP_GUARD_FLAG. The beforeSwap hook sets transient data per token pair. The same-transaction settlement reads fresh data. No stale reads possible because transient storage is per-transaction and overwritten per call.

hypotheses.title: View function inconsistency during swap (read-only reentrancy)
hypotheses.evidence: test_H5_view_function_post_swap_consistent: Post-swap pool state (reserves, sqrtPriceX96, liquidity) all consistent with token balances. Reserves updated atomically within the swap. View functions during callback would see intermediate state, but this is an external integrator concern (price oracle manipulation), not a protocol insolvency.

hypotheses.title: tokensOwed mapping key collision between LIQUIDITY_OWED and TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE
hypotheses.evidence: test_H6_no_storage_collision: LIQUIDITY_OWED=0x10, TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE=0x7F. Hook-managed fees use actual contract addresses as keys. Collision would require a hook deployed at address 0x10 or 0x7F (precompile range, impossible in practice). Different key types verified to produce different storage slots.

hypotheses.title: Sibling repo pool type state inconsistency across swap
hypotheses.evidence: test_H7_sibling_repo_state_consistency: Pool type's processSwapByInput called during swap correctly updates reserves and returns consistent amounts. Solvency check after swap confirms AMM balance >= reserves + fees. globalState[msg.sender] namespacing isolates each AMM's data.

hypotheses.title: Output swap solvency: hook fees added to amountOut create undercollateralization
hypotheses.evidence: test_H8_output_swap_solvency_analysis: Analyzed _applySwapByOutputOutputFees (line 2851-2895) which ADDS hook fees to amountOut. Pool type processes inflated amount. BUT _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse (line 2166) resets swapCache.amountOut = swapCache.adjustedAmountSpecified (user's original desired amount). User receives only their requested amount. Extra output stays in AMM backing tokensOwed. No insolvency.

ruled_out_vectors.reason: ENTERED bit in transient storage reentrancy guard persists through all external calls. CEI pattern in fee transfers. All entry points check ENTERED first.

Each swap operation writes its own transient data (beforeSwap overwrites per token). Second write intentionally overwrites first. No stale reads within same transaction because all paths re-read after hooks.

In Solidity, InternalSwapCache memory tmpSwapCache = swapCache creates a REFERENCE alias, not a copy. Both point to same memory. All mutations via tmpSwapCache automatically visible through swapCache. This is by-design, not a bug.

Forward routing: swapCache.amountIn = swapCache.amountOut (line 1469). Backward routing: swapCache.amountOut = swapCache.amountIn (line 1626). Both correctly propagate computed amounts as next hop input/output.

_applySwapByOutputOutputFees adds fees to amountOut for pool type processing. _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse (line 2166) resets amountOut to user original amount. Extra stays in AMM. No undercollateralization.
_depositWrappedNativeAndRefundExcess refunds excess before WETH deposit, but ENTERED bit blocks reentrancy. No value extraction possible via receive() callback.
Flash loan callback protected by FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG. Round-trip swap loses to fees. AMM solvency maintained after flashloan+swap sequences.
100-swap dust loop test shows total extraction after 100 swaps is less than initial deposit. Rounding consistently favors the AMM. No dust accumulation attack vector.
Two-pool arb test (swap A then B then A) always results in net loss to attacker due to fees and rounding. No value creation from cross-pool composition.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Queued hook fee double-collect via flag clearing
ruled_out_vectors.reason: _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers clears custom flags (line 3190) but preserves ENTERED bit. collectHookFeesByHook during callback falls through to direct transfer, but CEI in _transferHookFeesByHook decrements storage before safeTransfer. No double-collect.
_collectToken (line 2917) and finalization (line 2208) use exact balance checks that reject fee-on-transfer tokens. Protocol is incompatible with such tokens by design.
Token0 (input): alice loses exactly what AMM gains. Token1 (output): AMM loses exactly what recipient gains. Total system tokens conserved across all swap paths.
Tick crossing updates liquidity correctly. liquidityNet sums to zero across all ticks. Price moves in correct direction after swap.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Withdrawal guarantee after heavy swap activity
ruled_out_vectors.reason: After 5 random swaps, full liquidity removal succeeds and returns non-zero amounts. AMM never holds liquidity hostage.
Malicious ERC-777-like token attempting reentry during transfer callback is blocked by ENTERED bit. State remains consistent.

summary: Comprehensive state-desync audit of Limit Break AMM across all 5 target repos. 62 Forge tests covering all 25 C-STATE checklist items (24/25 completed, C20 Medusa skipped due to crytic-compile cancun incompatibility), all 8 injected hypotheses tested and ruled out, plus invariant probes (100-swap dust loop, transient slot theft). Zero Medium+ exploitable vulnerabilities found. The codebase demonstrates robust state management: TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags with ENTERED bit blocks all reentrant state-changing calls; CEI pattern in fee transfers prevents double-collect; output swap finalization correctly resets amountOut to user requested amount; Solidity memory reference aliases are used correctly throughout; settlement conservation verified across all swap paths. 15 distinct attack vectors systematically tested and ruled out with compiling Forge PoC tests.
